claim: The Colombo–Kandy road, begun in the 1820s and completed/bridged by 1832, functioned first as strategic-political integration infrastructure and also opened the Kandyan interior to plantation investment; connectivity inverted part of the defensive value of isolation.
bounded_by: Modern scholarly synthesis supports the mechanism; exact purpose wording should not be strengthened to A without a colonial-era order/report. Road purpose is not identical to the later railway's explicitly documented coffee-export purpose.
notes: Cross-reference plantation sequence; do not narrate twice.
